The H-pattern manual road gearbox requires a clutch to pull away from rest under the project's derivation rules. The established synchromesh construction settles ordinary running-shift technique as clutch-required under the project's derivation rules. The road car is described as a conventional manual rather than an electronically managed shift system; no automatic cut is part of the documented control arrangement. Manual blip is a downshift action and is not applicable to the upshift field. Automatic blip is a downshift action and is not applicable to the upshift field. Synchromesh construction settles ordinary running-shift clutch technique as required. Throttle lift is modeled only for upshifts in this schema. Automatic cut is modeled only for upshifts in this schema. The project's documented derivation for synchromesh records a manual downshift blip as optional: it eases the synchronizers but is not required for engagement. The documented road car is a conventional manual with no automatic throttle-blip system described. The reviewed source describes a conventional three-spoke leather steering wheel, supporting a round conventional rim rather than a GT-formula or open-top control face. The source describes a conventional road-car wheel and dash instrumentation, not a wheel-mounted display. A conventional three-spoke leather wheel is described; no open-top racing rim is documented. The reviewed sources did not establish the remaining technique and wheel fields, which stay unknown in the real-car baseline: /authentic_controls/transmission/shift_pattern, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/throttle_lift, /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/shift_lights.
